enquiry: We would like an optical measurement during yeast fermentation to help us follow growth and notice changes earlier. Our team has mentioned both a biomass signal and a metabolic signal, but these have not been defined as separate targets. The broth becomes more optically dense as the run develops. We need help turning this request into an initial feasibility study with useful reference measurements.

citations.quote: Raman spectroscopy can be used in the same reactor to provide a "molecular fingerprint" for direct detection of specific metabolites like glucose, acetate, or lactate. spectral_ranges.statement: Nominal UV-Vis range covers electronic transitions (high sensitivity in 190-360 nm); usable range depends on instrument and optical configuration.

citations.quote: Furthermore, observing Raman bands is often complicated by light scattering from the illuminating laser, and for many organic compounds, by the superposition of luminescence (fluorescence), which has a significantly higher intensity.
